tasks.title: ResolvedConfig.promoted_siblings field and with_promoted_siblings method
steps: Run `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib config::resolve::tests::with_promoted_siblings_overlays_without_mutating_original config::resolve::tests::promoted_siblings_field_is_pub_not_pub_crate` from /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto. Expected failure: `error[E0609]: no field \`promoted_siblings\` on type \`ResolvedConfig\`` and `error[E0599]: no method named \`with_promoted_siblings\` found for struct \`ResolvedConfig\``.

In config/resolve.rs, add `use std::collections::BTreeSet;` to the existing `use std::collections::BTreeMap;` import line (resolve.rs:1) -- change it to `use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};`.
Add a new field to the `ResolvedConfig` struct (resolve.rs:15-42), immediately after the existing `pub(crate) raw_groups: RawGroupTable,` line:
```rust
pub promoted_siblings: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)>>,
```
This field is `pub`, not `pub(crate)`, matching the existing `pub packages` field -- T15's end-to-end test lives in crates/callisto-graph/tests/ (an external integration-test crate) and reads `workspace.config.promoted_siblings` directly per AC-23, which a `pub(crate)` field would not permit.
In the `Ok(ResolvedConfig { .. })` literal at the end of `load` (resolve.rs:489-507), add a new field initializer immediately after `raw_groups,`:
```rust
promoted_siblings: BTreeMap::new(),
```
Add the new method inside `impl ResolvedConfig` (the block starting at resolve.rs:49-ish, alongside the existing `pub fn provenance`):
```rust
pub(crate) fn with_promoted_siblings(
    &self,
    promoted_siblings: BTreeMap<String, Vec<(PackageId, BTreeSet<Ecosystem>)>>,
) -> ResolvedConfig {
    let mut overlay = self.clone();
    overlay.promoted_siblings = promoted_siblings;
    overlay
}
```
`with_promoted_siblings` itself stays `pub(crate)` (only walk.rs calls it internally); only the `promoted_siblings` field needs to be `pub` for external test-crate reads. A full `self.clone()` plus single-field overwrite is required (not a cross-module struct-update literal) because `provenance` is a private field only this module can construct.

Run `cargo test -p callisto-graph --lib config::resolve::tests::with_promoted_siblings_overlays_without_mutating_original config::resolve::tests::promoted_siblings_field_is_pub_not_pub_crate` -- expected: `test result: ok. 2 passed`.

tasks.title: Closing task: update track-f-resolution-extraction.json's AC-F6 to the new call-site text
steps:
Add a failing shell-level check (no Rust test needed -- this is a JSON text edit). From /Users/gabe/Projects/callisto, run:
```
python3 -c "

d = json.load(open('.claude/specs/track-f-resolution-extraction.json'))

"
```

Expected failure: `AssertionError: new text missing` -- AC-F6's current `criterion` field still reads the pre-Result call-site text ending in `let pkg_override = resolve_package_config(&id, cfg);`, which also still contains BOTH stale substrings that must be removed by the fix below: (a) the exact stale binding `resolve_package_config(&id, cfg);` and (b) the stale prose fragment `replaced by a single call to resolve_package_config(&id, cfg).`.

Use a non-destructive raw-text replace, not a JSON parse-mutate-dump round-trip (which would reflow unrelated formatting in the file). In Python:
```python
import json
path = '.claude/specs/track-f-resolution-extraction.json'
raw = open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8').read()
d = json.loads(raw)
ac = next(a for a in d['acceptance_criteria'] if a['id'] == 'AC-F6')
old_text = ac['criterion']
new_text = (
    'The inline two-pass [[package]] lookup in walk.rs (lines 160-169, the two '
    'cfg.packages.iter().find(...) calls joined by .or_else, followed by '
    '.map(|(_, cfg)| cfg)) is removed and replaced by a single call to '
    'resolve_package_config(&id, &cfg_with_local_promotions)?. The trailing '
    '.map(|(_, cfg)| cfg) at line 169 is deleted because resolve_package_config '
    'already returns Result<Option<&PackageConfig>, GraphError>, not '
    'Option<&(PackageId, PackageConfig)>. The resulting binding is: let '
    'pkg_override = resolve_package_config(&id, &cfg_with_local_promotions)?;, '
    'where cfg_with_local_promotions is the build-local ResolvedConfig overlay '
    'constructed via cfg.with_promoted_siblings(...) per '
    'SPEC-TRACK3B1-IDENTITY-PROMOTION-CORE. All tests in '
    'crates/callisto-graph/tests/per_package_config_test.rs pass without modification.'
)
old_escaped = json.dumps(old_text)[1:-1]
new_escaped = json.dumps(new_text)[1:-1]
assert raw.count(old_escaped) == 1, f'expected exactly one occurrence of the old escaped criterion text, found {raw.count(old_escaped)}'
raw2 = raw.replace(old_escaped, new_escaped, 1)
open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(raw2)
print('replaced')
```
This edits only the AC-F6 `criterion` string's bytes in place, leaving every other byte of the file -- indentation, key order, every other criterion -- untouched.

goal: Implement ecosystem-prefixed identity resolution and cross-ecosystem name promotion in callisto-graph, so colliding package names across fully disjoint ecosystems (e.g. a Cargo crate and an npm platform-native binding sharing a bare name) promote to distinct PackageId::Prefixed identities instead of erroring, while genuinely ambiguous or same-ecosystem collisions still fail closed.
architecture: ManifestWalkResolver::build gains per-path bookkeeping (claiming_ecosystems, path_native_keys, primary_ecosystems) and a promotion predicate (disjoint claiming-ecosystem sets) applied both at the by-path collision point and when a later path joins an already-promoted name; five STALE-KEY REWRITE locations keep IdentityIndex's bare/native/platform/prefixed maps and package_manifest_decls consistent under promotion. ResolvedConfig gains a promoted_siblings field (populated after ManifestWalkResolver::build returns, inside Workspace::load) and a build-local overlay method (with_promoted_siblings) so resolve_package_config can detect and reject config rules that are now ambiguous across promoted siblings, both during build() and during aggregate().
